exemplar.title: What strong work looks like
exemplar.intro: Here is how a strong maker explains a different project — cutting ribbon for a gift-wrap station — so you can copy the moves, not the numbers.

traits.trait: Names the operation and the reciprocal
traits.sample: To cut 6 feet of ribbon into 1/3-foot bows, I divided 6 by 1/3, which means multiplying by the reciprocal: 6 × 3 = 18 bows.
traits.why: Showing the reciprocal step in words is what the fraction-division rubric row calls expert work.

traits.trait: Turns the remainder into a real length
traits.sample: I got 10 2/5 pieces, so the leftover is 2/5 of one piece. Each piece is 1/2 foot, so the scrap is 2/5 × 1/2 = 1/5 foot.
traits.why: Separating 'fraction of a piece' from 'physical scrap length' is exactly what the Scrap and Remainders row rewards.

traits.sample: The thin 1/3-foot bows gave me the most pieces, because a smaller divisor always makes a bigger quotient.
traits.why: Stating the pattern, not just the count, earns top marks on the Reflection row.

traits.sample: Eighteen bows from 6 feet makes sense, because each foot of ribbon holds exactly 3 bows.
traits.why: A quick per-unit check proves the quotient was verified, not just calculated.
